Chowbus is a leading Asian restaurant technology SaaS platform, with deep roots in the North American market for years. Currently, we stand as a pioneering enterprise in the North American Asian Restaurant SaaS sector. Driven by precise market positioning and efficient product services, our business has achieved doubled growth annually, covering over 30 core states and 100 key cities across the U.S., and partnering with more than 10,000 Asian restaurants. We build tech ecosystems that help restaurants grow, serve with heart, and uplift their communities，our vision is to creat a world where culturally rooted food entrepreneurs thrive everywhere.

Our sales team is scaling fast, and we need an Early Talent Recruiter to help us find the next generation of talent at universities across the U.S. and Canada.

Love connecting people? Know every CSSA, WeChat group, and campus event worth knowing? This role turns what you're best at into your career.

What You'll Focus On

- Build and own campus recruiting across U.S. and Canadian universities, focused on early-career sales talent
- Own full-cycle recruiting for GTM roles across the U.S. and Canada, including Sales Managers, Sales Associates, POS Technicians, and more, from sourcing and outreach to interview scheduling and offer
- Grow Chowbus's presence in Chinese student communities: Chinese Students and Scholars Associations (CSSAs), Chinese and Asian student associations, alumni networks, WeChat groups, and career centers

- Create recruiting content in Chinese and English, including posts, posters, and short videos, that students actually want to read and share
- Partner with Marketing on employer branding, including recruiting posters, copy, short videos, and online campaigns
- Plan and run campus events, info sessions, and career fairs, in person and online
- Build a campus ambassador network to extend our reach at target schools
- Screen candidates, coordinate interviews, and deliver a fast, warm experience from first touch to offer
- Coordinate across time zones with our recruiting team in China and with hiring managers to keep every hiring process moving efficiently
- Build and maintain a talent pool to support ongoing sales hiring
- Track results by school and channel in our ATS and reporting tools, figure out what works, and keep experimenting
- Find new ways to hire smarter: build relationships with recruiting agencies, test new AI tools, and try anything that makes our recruiting more efficient. You're encouraged to experiment
- Partner closely with hiring managers and Sales leadership to understand hiring needs, refine candidate profiles, and help shape our talent strategy

In your first 30 days:

- Learn our sales roles, hiring process, and tools
- Build a target school list and secure Handshake approvals at priority schools
- Establish relationships with student organizations at our priority target schools

In your first 60 days:

- Run campus events or info sessions each recruiting season
- Build a steady pipeline of qualified early-career sales candidates
- Launch a recurring content presence on WeChat and Xiaohongshu that drives applications

- Run full-cycle searches for GTM roles independently, from intake meeting to accepted offer
- Close your first 5 hires through campus and early-career channels
- Launch an employer branding campaign together with Marketing
- Share a channel performance review with recommendations for the next quarter

- Strong command of WeChat and Xiaohongshu (RED), including community management and creating content that gets engagement
- Comfortable with LinkedIn and Handshake for outreach and job search
- Familiarity with the job search process for students, including work authorization questions international students face
- Organized with data: able to track pipelines in Google Sheets or Excel

- Bonus: Canva or CapCut, an ATS such as Greenhouse, LinkedIn Recruiter, virtual event platforms, or AI tools for content creation

At Caterpillar, technology always has a purpose, which is to solve our customers’ toughest challenges. Through Cat Technology, we are solving problems by building the intelligence layer that connects machines, data, and people to make jobsites safer, more productive, and more sustainable. By combining deep domain expertise in physical systems with software, connectivity, autonomy, and AI, we deliver solutions that work in the real world—on real jobsites, at global scale.

You’ll build and deploy against one of the most unique data foundations—over 1.6 million connected assets generating real-world data daily.  These data and platform capabilities are enabling the development of AI models, edge computing architectures, and software systems that scale across fleets, products, and industries. The result will be a new generation of machines that continuously learn, improve, and deliver performance at scale.

Be Part of What’s Next in Autonomous Construction Sites

Construction autonomy is one of the most complex challenges in applied AI, and at Caterpillar, advancements in physical AI, simulation, sensing, and edge computing are turning things that once felt impossible—intelligent machines operating in dynamic jobsites—into reality.

Our connected ecosystem brings together massive volumes of high-quality data to create a foundation where engineers like you can build and deploy against.

If this work motivates you, we invite you to join our team. In these roles, you’ll work at the intersection of the physical and digital worlds. You’ll help design and deliver intelligent systems that enable machines to perceive their environment, make informed decisions, and support safer, more productive operations.

Apply today to build the new era of construction autonomy at Caterpillar.

Job Summary:

The Digital Twin Architect owns what is in our virtual world and how faithful it is — the machine, the jobsite, the sensors, and the live data that keeps them honest.

The Principal Digital Architect – Digital Twin is responsible for the architecture of the digital twins that Physical AI, simulation, and autonomy are developed and validated against. This spans three twin families: machine twins (kinematics, multibody dynamics, hydraulics, powertrain, implements and tools, and their interaction with material), jobsite / environment twins (terrain and design surfaces from survey, drone photogrammetry and LiDAR scans, GIS and geospatial data, site infrastructure, dynamic site state, weather and lighting), and sensor twins (camera, LiDAR, radar, GNSS, IMU models mounted in their true frames on the machine). Each twin must be simulation-ready, physically based, versioned, and validated against the real machine and site.

The architect defines the asset and scene pipeline that turns CAD, PLM, survey, and reality-capture data into simulation-ready OpenUSD assets and environments for NVIDIA Omniverse / Isaac Sim and Unreal Engine; the data model that connects twins to machine telemetry and fleet data so twins reflect the as-operated machine and as-built site; the validation and correlation program (test data correlation, scenario-based testing, regression testing, telematics comparison) that quantifies twin fidelity; and the synthetic data and neural reconstruction (3D Gaussian Splatting, NeRF, real-to-sim) workflows that scale twin creation. The role works closely with the Simulation Engine architect, who owns the runtime the twins execute in, and with the AI Factory architect, who consumes twin-generated data.

This role bridges architecture and engineering: translating the digital twin vision into detailed solution designs, reusable patterns, standards, and implementation guidance, and guiding the engineering teams that build them.

What You Will Do:

- Developing detailed architecture deliverables to solve business problems.

- Designing an application's technical infrastructure, such as specific databases, programming languages, utilities, and testing approaches.

- Leading the evaluation and deployment of new technologies to add or enhance existing digital technical capabilities.

- Participating in addressing business requirements for applications and collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver digital solutions that meets business results.

What You Will Have:

- Requirements Analysis: Knowledge of tools, methods, and techniques of requirement analysis; ability to elicit, analyze and record required business functionality and non-functionality requirements to ensure the success of a system or software development project.

- Analytical Thinking: Knowledge of techniques and tools that promote effective analysis; ability to determine the root cause of organizational problems and create alternative solutions that resolve these problems.

- Platform Architecture: Knowledge of technologies and methods to design processing mechanisms and roadmaps to execute business application systems; ability to design these roadmaps and deploy supportive interfaces for end-users to access related systems, in accordance with standards and processes.

- Target Architecture: Knowledge of target architecture; ability to develop the IT blueprint and roadmap while aligning the architecture and processes with business strategies and objectives.

- Effective Communications: Understanding of effective communication concepts, tools and techniques; ability to effectively transmit, receive, and accurately interpret ideas, information, and needs through the application of appropriate communication behaviors.

Top Candidates Will Have: -

- Digital Twin Platforms – Delivering physically based digital twins of machines, vehicles, robots, or industrial sites used for simulation, validation, or AI training, including twin fidelity tiers, versioning, and lifecycle.

- NVIDIA Omniverse and OpenUSD – Hands-on Omniverse (Kit, Isaac Sim, Replicator, Nucleus) and OpenUSD (composition, schemas, USD Physics, SimReady assets); CAD-to-USD conversion at scale; Unreal Engine or Unity for large outdoor environments.

- Machine and Physics Modeling – Multibody dynamics, articulations, hydraulics, powertrain, and implement-material interaction in URDF / MJCF / USD Physics; model calibration and system identification against measured data; CAE / PLM exposure (Siemens NX, Ansys, Modelica, Adams) a plus.

- Jobsite, Terrain, and Geospatial Twins – Building 3D environments from drone photogrammetry, LiDAR, survey and design surfaces, and GIS data; procedural site generation; construction or mining site data (Trimble, Topcon, Hexagon, Cat MineStar / Grade) highly desirable.

- Sensor Twins and Synthetic Data – Physically based camera, LiDAR, radar, GNSS, IMU models with calibration frames and environmental effects; synthetic data with ground truth and domain randomization (Omniverse Replicator).

- Neural Reconstruction and Real-to-Sim – 3D Gaussian Splatting, NeRF, or world foundation models (e.g. NVIDIA Cosmos) to create sensor-realistic environments from fleet data, combined with physics-based twins.

- Connected Twin Data – Data models and pipelines linking twins to live machine telemetry and fleet data (ROS 2, MQTT, Kafka, DDS; edge-to-cloud) for event replay and twin validation.

- Sim-to-Real Validation – Established acceptance criteria for twin fidelity: test data correlation, scenario-based and regression testing, HIL / SIL correlation, quantified sim-to-real gap metrics.

- Software Engineering – Strong Python and C++; GPU / CUDA workloads, containers and Kubernetes, CI/CD, cloud (AWS / Azure); comfort with AI coding tools.

- Architecture Leadership – Translates architecture into implementation plans, reusable patterns, and standards across teams; technical leadership of engineers.

- Domain Exposure – Off-highway, construction, mining, or agriculture machines, or digital twin programs at NVIDIA, Applied Intuition, Volvo Autonomous Solutions, Komatsu, John Deere, Siemens, or Duality AI.

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or related field; master’s or doctoral degree preferred.

Why Caterpillar

You'll work on some of the most challenging applications of AI in the physical world, helping build systems that transform vast amounts of machine and sensor data into the intelligence that powers autonomous and AI-enabled equipment. If you're excited about applying AI to real-world machines operating in complex environments, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply today to build the new era of construction autonomy at Caterpillar.

Job Summary:

The Learning Systems Architect owns how the machine learns — the end-to-end system that turns simulation, digital twins, and fleet data into high-performance, field-proven policies and models.

The Principal Architect – Reinforcement Learning (RL) Systems is responsible for the architecture of the learning system that produces Caterpillar’s Physical AI models: the reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and foundation-model post-training pipelines that train perception, prediction, planning, and control policies for excavators, dozers, loaders, and haul trucks. Top Candidates Will Have:

- Imitation Learning and Foundation-Model Post-Training – Behavior cloning, offline RL (IQL, GAIL), distillation, diffusion policies; vision-language-action or robot foundation models with RL-based post-training (RLHF / DPO / GRPO).

As Product Counsel, you will be a hands-on legal partner to the teams building Claude for consumers and businesses. You'll work across Claude's apps, subscriptions, growth programs and enterprise offerings, moving to wherever the need is greatest. You'll learn from experienced product lawyers, get close to the product quickly, and take on more ownership as you go. This is a generalist role for someone who wants range, likes a fast pace, and is ready to do the routine work and the novel work with the same care.

- Pick up new areas as priorities shift, and help with incidents and escalations when they come up

- Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you'll be based
- At least 4 years of relevant legal experience, with exposure to technology, consumer or regulated products

Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. Company Description
Etsy is the global marketplace for unique and creative goods. We build, power, and evolve the tools and technologies that connect millions of entrepreneurs with millions of buyers around the world. What’s the role?

We’re looking for a Senior Staff Quantitative UX Researcher to help lead a quantitative research practice within the Product Research team and work horizontally across the buyer experience - grounded in rigorous survey design, statistical analysis, and experimental methods.

This is a highly collaborative and influential individual contributor role. You will work across Etsy with Product, Design, Engineering, Analytics, and other researchers, translating quantitative evidence into clear priorities, standards, and recommendations.

What’s this team like at Etsy?

- Our research team focuses on using research to guide the development of buyer and seller experiences in our dynamic marketplace of unique items. Our insights are part of the vernacular at Etsy and play a key role in building confidence around product decisions and our overall business strategy.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Our Strategic Deals team originates, structures, negotiates, and closes the deals that secure the compute Anthropic uses to train and serve frontier AI systems. We work closely with engineering, infrastructure, finance, legal, product, and go-to-market teams to expand Anthropic's access to cloud capacity, silicon, networking, and the financing behind them.

We are hiring several Strategic Deals Leads focused on compute and infrastructure. In this role, you will source opportunities, design partnerships, and negotiate high-value agreements with some of the world's largest technology companies, and you will connect deal terms to structured finance solutions. Your work will directly shape how quickly and reliably Anthropic can bring new compute online.

Each hire will bring deep expertise in one or more of these areas while working across the broader infrastructure stack:

- Cloud compute: building and running a pipeline of capacity across established and emerging cloud providers, and structuring the financing that connects capacity commitments to their economics.
- Compute infrastructure: going deep into the silicon supply chain, structuring co-development and early-access deals with semiconductor and emerging hardware companies, and securing networking, backbone, and memory supply.
- Compute partnerships: owning multi-year partnerships with the largest cloud providers, where compute commitments, financing structures, model availability on partner platforms, marketplace and co-sell arrangements, and pricing and revenue-share constructs are negotiated together.

Key responsibilities

- Own deals end to end in your focus area, from opportunity identification and term sheet development through diligence, negotiation, internal approval, close, and post-close execution
- Lead negotiations for complex, high-value agreements with hyperscalers and other cloud providers, semiconductor and hardware suppliers, networking and memory vendors, data center operators, and emerging infrastructure companies
- Bring capital markets and financing thinking to every transaction, including vendor financing, equipment leasing, capacity prepayments, project finance, and credit and residual value guarantees
- Build financial models, term analyses, and commercial frameworks that compare supply options and give leadership a clear view of value, tradeoffs, and risk-adjusted outcomes
- Partner with engineering and infrastructure teams to understand future workload requirements and translate them into long-term supply strategies and commercially viable deal terms
- Build and own senior relationships with commercial, finance, product, and legal counterparts across the AI infrastructure ecosystem
- Drive internal alignment with legal, finance, engineering, product, and go-to-market teams on deal terms, risk parameters, and the approval path for large commitments
- Track market, technology, competitive, and financing developments across AI infrastructure, including supply constraints, and turn them into clear recommendations for senior leadership
- Represent Anthropic externally with corporate executives, investment banks, and infrastructure investors involved in our transactions

Minimum qualifications

- A track record of originating, structuring, negotiating, and closing complex, high-value technology, infrastructure, or capacity transactions as the principal and lead negotiator (not in a supporting or advisory capacity) and the ability to operate independently from day one
- Transactional experience in at least one focus area: cloud capacity or data center transactions, semiconductor and hardware supply (accelerators, CPU, memory, or networking, including backbone), or hyperscaler and cloud partnerships
- Working knowledge of how large infrastructure commitments are financed, such as vendor financing, take-or-pay obligations, equipment leasing, or project finance, and the ability to shape financing terms alongside commercial terms
- Financial modeling skills to build and pressure-test the economics of large infrastructure transactions
- Experience developing term sheets and negotiating definitive agreements alongside legal counsel
- Ability to work with technical teams and translate engineering requirements into deal structures, contract terms, and strategic business recommendations
- Experience negotiating agreements that combine infrastructure or capacity terms with commercial, product, or go-to-market terms, and an understanding of how those components interact
- Experience building partnerships and influencing senior stakeholders across internal and external organizations, including executive leadership

Preferred qualifications

- 8–10+ years of experience in strategic deals, corporate development, partnerships, investment banking, or business development at technology companies, hyperscalers, cloud providers, or financial institutions, with direct transactional ownership

- Direct experience working with or inside a hyperscaler on AI or cloud partnerships, including familiarity with model gardens, marketplaces, co-sell programs, and partner economics

- Experience managing multiple high-value transactions simultaneously at different stages of maturity and commercial development

- Comfort operating in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where market structures, provider economics, and partnership norms are still evolving

- A genuine interest in the future of AI infrastructure and in Anthropic's mission of building safe, beneficial AI

We're hiring for several roles on this team. Apply once, and we'll match you to the focus area that best fits your background.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$265,000—$325,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
